messages.content:
Read one passage of a document about machines at work (law, manual, guidance, internal guideline,
plant record) and write down the important facts it states.

Answer with one line per fact, fields separated by " | ", nothing else, no header, no code fence:
subject | predicate | object | condition | quote
- predicate: a short camelCase verb phrase of your choice.
- condition: any condition or exception, or "" if none.
- quote: the words of the passage the fact comes from.
At most 12 facts. If the passage states nothing important, answer with the single word NONE.

Passage: DIR, Annex I, 5.5

5.5. FIRE The second indent of section 3.5.2 is mandatory in respect of machinery which comprises highly flammable parts. The braking system of machinery intended for use in underground workings must be designed and constructed in such a way that it does not produce sparks or cause fires. Machinery with internal combustion engines for use in underground workings must be fitted only with engines using fuel with a low vaporising pressure and which exclude any spark of electrical origin.

Braking system of machinery for underground workings | mustBeDesignedToAvoid | producing sparks or causing fires | machinery is intended for use in underground workings | "The braking system of machinery intended for use in underground workings must be designed and constructed in such a way that it does not produce sparks or cause fires."
Machinery with internal combustion engines for underground workings | mustBeFittedWith | only engines using fuel with a low vaporising pressure | machinery is for use in underground workings | "Machinery with internal combustion engines for use in underground workings must be fitted only with engines using fuel with a low vaporising pressure and which exclude any spark of electrical origin."
Engines fitted to machinery for underground workings | mustExclude | any spark of electrical origin | machinery is for use in underground workings | "Machinery with internal combustion engines for use in underground workings must be fitted only with engines using fuel with a low vaporising pressure and which exclude any spark of electrical origin."
